result.title: Recasting Visual Language Models as EEG Foundation Models for Clinical Neurodiagnostics
result.summary: Historically automated electroencephalography (EEG) systems was done using task-specific supervised models trained on purposely annotated data. A more recent modeling paradigm relies on creating a unified representation, or a 'foundation model', for multiple modality-specific tasks through large-scale domain-specific pretraining on the unannotated EEG signal. The quality of this unified representation directly depends on the availability of the modality-specific datasets. At the same time, generalist Vision Language Models (VLMs) exhibit broad few-shot learning capacities as well as good fine-tuning adaptability to different visual and language tasks. Can VLMs learn how to read and interpret EEG visually, emulating to a degree the way human clinicians inspect the EEG patterns? In this work we make a case that they can: we show that generalist VLMs without large-scale EEG pretraining perform competitively across a collection of clinical neuro-diagnostic tasks, can adapt to different tasks in a few-shot learning setting better than specialist foundation models, and exhibit better performance with model scaling when modality-specific models fail to exhibit.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作将 EEG 信号以可视图像形式输入通用 VLM，在多个临床神经诊断任务上评测，并与无标注 EEG 大规模预训练得到的专用基础模型比较 few-shot 适应能力及随模型规模扩展的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 它提供了「通用 VLM 视觉表示能否直接承载非自然、细粒度信号证据」以及「能否以 few-shot 替代领域大规模预训练」的对照线索，可供核查与 LVR 中视觉细节保留、训练监督成本权衡的关系。
